_raSoatSkill4d.1_vatTacDongCoThe: Khong co vat tac dong len nguoi. Cai dua tac dong len RANG cua ham (C2-46) — ve ban tay + ham, khong lo mat.
_raSoatSkill4d.2_trangThaiNhanVat: Woodward hai moc: 1912 (C2-07b) va ve huu 1924-44 (C2-55) — hai asset rieng (skill 5b). Dawson chet 1916 va Woodward chet 1944: KHONG ve canh chet, dung lai chan dung, nam la chu hau ky.
_raSoatSkill4d.3_nguoiCoThatDuocGoiTen: Charles Dawson (anh studio + tranh 1915), Arthur Smith Woodward (anh ~1900s + tranh 1915 + anh luc gia), Kenneth Oakley (anh 1949, 1953, 1957), Joseph Weiner (chi co anh luc ~55-60 -> ve tre lai, giu kinh gong sung). Nguoi KHONG duoc loi ke goi ten -> figure minh hoa: linh muc tre (Teilhard), nguoi lam cong (Hargreaves), giao su King's College (Waterston), nha giai phau Nam Phi (Dart), nhom 2016, nha khao co (Miles Russell).
_raSoatSkill4d.4_tenSaiThoiKy: Khong co ten doi theo thoi ky can doi hinh. 'Natural History Museum' — nam 1912 ten chinh thuc la British Museum (Natural History), cung toa nha 1881; ve toa nha, khong ghi chu. Ban do the gioi dung bien gioi 1898 (giong 1913) vi Phap 1913 chua co Alsace-Lorraine.
_raSoatSkill4d.5_trangThaiGoc: Manh so (C2-04e) -> nhieu manh (C2-06) -> bo Piltdown 2 (C2-23) -> manh nut co soi (C2-50b). Ban phuc dung (C2-16) -> trong tu kinh (C2-28b) -> tach roi (C2-41). Rang trang tinh tinh (C2-36b) -> dua (C2-36) -> nhuom (C2-36c) -> giong het Piltdown (C2-37).
_raSoatSkill4d.6_choNoi: Rang gan vao ho bang chat tram (C2-50c); soi nhet vao ke nut (C2-50b) — cho noi la chu the.
_raSoatSkill4d.7_nhayCoc: Them C2-10b (Dawson mot minh nhat manh xuong — loi ke khang dinh 'found by Dawson alone'). KHONG them canh Dawson dua/nhuom ham truoc khi loi ke tiet lo (lo loi giai som); hanh vi gia mao chi o C2-46 sau tiet lo, va chi ve ban tay.
_raSoatSkill4d.8_hanhViNoi: Dawson ke (C2-04d, dung lai cho 'Dawson said', 'Dawson reported'), Woodward cong bo (C2-14) va phat bieu (C2-19c), giao su lap luan (C2-20), Weiner noi voi Oakley (C2-34b, co nguoi nghe). Noi dung loi noi (ham dat canh so) KHONG ve thanh canh — ham va manh so la phan tu roi.
_raSoatSkill4d.9_mucChacChan: 'According to Dawson' / 'Dawson said' / 'Dawson reported': KHONG ve canh nguoi lam cong trao manh so, khong ve canh dap so, khong ve canh Dawson tim ra Piltdown 2 — chi ve Dawson dang noi + hien vat. Qua dua (C2-05) chi la vat minh hoa cum tu. 'as if someone had ground them' la gia thuyet cua Weiner — dung lai can canh rang (C2-13), khong ve canh mai.
_raSoatSkill4d.10_trungChucNang_dungLai: Xem _dungLai. BO: ngoi nha Woodward mua gan Piltdown (khong co anh that), canh hoi nghi 1953 (bao chi C2-03d da ganh), co Phap/My (ban do C2-21 da ganh), toa nha Liverpool John Moores (nhom C2-48 da ganh), so do nga rang (X-quang C2-39 da ganh).
_raSoatSkill4d.11_netMat: Net mat trung tinh mac dinh o moi shot. Khong gan tam trang dac y cho Dawson o C2-10b, khong gan ve phan khich cho Woodward.

_thuNghiem: C2-08b la shot mention BON chip (3 nguoi + 1 noi chon) — nhieu nhat tu truoc toi gio; soi mat co lan nhau khong. C2-47, C2-49, C2-51 dung kind 'symbol' (khong co styleByKind) de khoi bi noi luat mat don gian vao bong nguoi.
_anhChung: Mọi ảnh vẽ theo nét của ba ảnh neo phong cách Tú gửi — viền mực đen dày không đều, tô màu phẳng, gạch chì thấy nét, nền trắng trơn — khổ 16:9. Người có MẶT ĐƠN GIẢN: mắt chấm nhỏ, mũi ngắn, miệng một nét (hoặc hình mở khi đang nói/cười), không đổ bóng trên mặt. Shot vẽ bằng CHỮ thì runner tự đính một ảnh neo theo loại (một người → 02, nhóm → 03, đồ vật/nơi chốn → 01). Shot @MENTION chỉ dùng ảnh được gọi tên trong câu. HIỆN VẬT THẬT (hàm, mảnh sọ, sọ Taung) có ảnh chụp trong refs/case-2 — lúc dựng có thể chèn ảnh thật cạnh bản vẽ. Hộp sọ và sọ hoá thạch KHÔNG dùng làm thumbnail.

_dungLai.at: He found Roman figurines, Stone Age hand axes, and ancient wooden boats, so many remarkable things that the newspapers nicknamed him "the Wizard of Sussex."
_dungLai.lyDo: Chan dung Dawson; biet danh la chu hau ky.

_dungLai.at: Dawson said the workmen had smashed an entire skull, thinking it was a fossilized coconut.
_dungLai.cue: Dawson said the workmen had smashed an entire skull
_dungLai.lyDo: Dawson dang ke + manh so. KHONG ve canh dap vo (loi Dawson).

_dungLai.at: The most important pieces, more of the skull and half of a lower jaw, were all found by Dawson alone.
It was the jaw that stunned the scientific world.
_dungLai.cue: It was the jaw that stunned the scientific world

_dungLai.at: On December 18th, 1912, at a meeting of the Geological Society of London, Woodward announced a new species of early human.
_dungLai.cue: a meeting of the Geological Society of London

_dungLai.at: He gave it the scientific name Eoanthropus dawsoni, meaning "Dawson's dawn man."
_dungLai.cue: He gave it the scientific name
_dungLai.lyDo: Ten khoa hoc la chu hau ky.

_dungLai.at: His reconstruction showed a skull much like a modern human's, with a brain about two-thirds the size of ours, attached to the jaw of an ape.
_dungLai.cue: attached to the jaw of an ape

_dungLai.at: It fit perfectly with what many experts in England believed at the time, that as our ancestors became human, the brain grew large first and everything else followed.
The newspapers called it the missing link between apes and humans.
That same year, an anatomy professor at King's College London argued in the journal Nature that this was simply an ape's jaw lying next to a human skull.
_dungLai.cue: simply an ape's jaw lying next to a human skull
_dungLai.lyDo: Ham + manh so dat canh nhau o hau ky (noi dung lap luan, khong ve thanh canh).

_dungLai.at: But their voices were drowned out.
_dungLai.cue: But their voices were drowned out

_dungLai.at: In 1915, Dawson reported finding a second skull, which became known as Piltdown 2, at another site about 2 miles away.
The exact location was never recorded.
_dungLai.cue: The exact location was never recorded
_dungLai.lyDo: Canh dong chung chung; dau hoi la hau ky.

_dungLai.at: For many people who were still on the fence, 2 separate finds at 2 separate sites made Piltdown much harder to dismiss.
In August 1916, Charles Dawson died.
_dungLai.lyDo: KHONG ve canh chet: chan dung + nam la chu hau ky.

_dungLai.at: From that day on, the Piltdown gravel pit never produced another piece of bone.
_dungLai.cue: never produced another piece of bone

_dungLai.at: In 1924, an anatomist in South Africa announced the fossil of a young ancient ape-human with a small skull but a very humanlike jaw and teeth, the exact opposite of Piltdown.
_dungLai.lyDo: So Taung canh ban phuc dung Piltdown.

_dungLai.at: His discovery was brushed aside for years, partly because it didn't fit with Piltdown.
_dungLai.lyDo: So Taung; dau X la hau ky neu can.

_dungLai.at: In the late 1940s, Kenneth Oakley, a geologist at the Natural History Museum, tried out a new technique.
_dungLai.cue: a geologist at the Natural History Museum

_dungLai.at: The results showed that the Piltdown bones were far younger than the age everyone had given them.
_dungLai.cue: far younger than the age everyone had given them

_dungLai.at: Weiner went back through the reports and the casts of the fossils, and he noticed that the 2 molars were worn down just a little too evenly, as if someone had ground them with something.
_dungLai.cue: worn down just a little too evenly
_dungLai.lyDo: Can canh rang ham mon phang.

_dungLai.at: X-rays showed that no new dentin had grown in beneath the worn surface, which meant the wear hadn't happened while the owner of those teeth was alive.
In November 1953, the findings were made public.
The methods used on Piltdown 1 and Piltdown 2 were the same, from the way the bones were stained, to the gravel packed into their cracks, to the dental putty used to fix the teeth in place.
The methods used on Piltdown 1 and Piltdown 2 were the same, from the way the bones were stained, to the gravel packed into their cracks, to the dental putty used to fix the teeth in place.
_dungLai.cue: the way the bones were stained

_dungLai.at: DNA analysis even showed that the teeth from both sites came from the same orangutan.
The team concluded that the forger was Charles Dawson.
_dungLai.lyDo: Bong nguoi -> chan dung Dawson (hau ky dung cap nay).

_dungLai.at: Another archaeologist went back through Dawson's lifelong collection and counted at least 38 fakes.
_dungLai.lyDo: Tu do co; con so 38 la chu hau ky.

_dungLai.at: The one person who never found out was Arthur Smith Woodward.
_dungLai.cue: never found out was Arthur Smith Woodward

_dungLai.at: When he retired in 1924, he bought a house near Piltdown, and for the next 20 years he kept digging in that same gravel pit, the one that hadn't given up a single bone since the day Dawson died.
_dungLai.cue: he bought a house near Piltdown
_dungLai.lyDo: Woodward gia — bo shot ngoi nha (khong co anh that).

_dungLai.at: Woodward passed away in 1944, 9 years before Piltdown Man was exposed.
_dungLai.lyDo: KHONG ve canh chet: chan dung + nam la chu hau ky.
